data.rule: The app may only share user data acquired via Apple Pay with third parties to facilitate or improve delivery of goods and services.

items.label: Digital goods follow Guideline 3.1

items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Software offered under this rule must follow Guideline 3.1 in order to offer digital goods or services to end users.

items.label: Digital goods must use Apple payment system
items.claim: Digital subscriptions and in-app purchases are not allowed unless they go through the Apple payment system.
items.use_note: Use to route digital goods only through Apple payment system.

data.rule: Digital subscriptions and in-app purchases must go through the Apple payment system, and the app must not offer other payment routes for them.

items.label: No buttons or links to non-IAP purchases
items.claim: Apple's guidelines say apps may not include buttons, links or calls-to-action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms other than In-App Purchase.
items.use_note: Use to avoid buttons or links to non-IAP purchases.

data.rule: The app must not include buttons, links or calls-to-action that send customers to purchasing mechanisms other than In-App Purchase.

items.label: External links allowed for non-digital goods

items.label: Web checkout outside app allowed

items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: Ordering inside the app cannot be done, so the app may direct users to complete transactions outside the app on the mobile site.

items.label: Webview and redirect workarounds risk rejection

items.use_note: Use to avoid webview or redirect workarounds that risk rejection.

data.rule: The app must not use webviews, deep links or browser redirects to work around payment restrictions.

items.label: Google Play in-app billing usage scope

data.rule: Google Play in-app billing may be used for virtual game products, app functionality such as unlocking features, subscriptions, and cloud software products.

items.label: Disclose store-processed in-app purchases in terms
items.claim: If an app has in-app purchases that go through an app store, the app must disclose this to users in its Terms and Conditions agreement.
items.use_note: Use to disclose store-processed purchases in terms and conditions.

data.rule: The app must disclose to users in its Terms and Conditions that in-app purchases go through an app store such as Apple App Store or Google Play Store.

items.label: Apple requires its in-app purchase function
items.claim: Apple's guidelines say developers must use Apple's in-app purchase function for things like unlocking app features or functionalities.
items.use_note: Use for Apple in-app purchase requirement for unlocking features.

data.rule: Developers must use Apple's in-app purchase function to unlock app features or functionalities such as subscriptions, in-game currencies, game levels, access to premium content, or a full version.

items.label: Explain unreviewable in-app purchase items

data.rule: Explain in the review notes any configured in-app purchase item that cannot be found or reviewed in the app.

items.label: Disclose additional purchases in metadata

data.rule: The app description, screenshots and previews must clearly indicate whether featured items, levels, subscriptions or similar require additional purchases.

items.label: Explain non-obvious in-app purchases in review notes

items.use_note: Rule from the platform: apply it to permissions, build setup and store review.

data.rule: The app must include detailed explanations of non-obvious features and in-app purchases in the App Review notes.

items.label: Tell users which content needs purchase

platform_constraints.rule: The app must disclose to users in its Terms and Conditions that in-app purchases go through an app store such as Apple App Store or Google Play Store.
Explain in the review notes any configured in-app purchase item that cannot be found or reviewed in the app.
The app description, screenshots and previews must clearly indicate whether featured items, levels, subscriptions or similar require additional purchases.
The app must include detailed explanations of non-obvious features and in-app purchases in the App Review notes.
The app must communicate to users which creator content requires additional purchases.
Digital subscriptions and in-app purchases must go through the Apple payment system, and the app must not offer other payment routes for them.
The app must not include buttons, links or calls-to-action that send customers to purchasing mechanisms other than In-App Purchase.
The app may include external payment links only for non-digital goods or services such as physical products, memberships or event tickets.
Ordering inside the app cannot be done, so the app may direct users to complete transactions outside the app on the mobile site.
The app must not use webviews, deep links or browser redirects to work around payment restrictions.
Developers must use Apple's in-app purchase function to unlock app features or functionalities such as subscriptions, in-game currencies, game levels, access to premium content, or a full version.
Google Play in-app billing may be used for virtual game products, app functionality such as unlocking features, subscriptions, and cloud software products.
The app must not monetize built-in hardware or operating system capabilities such as Push Notifications, the camera or the gyroscope.
The app must not require payment or indirectly monetize access to the Apple Music service, such as through in-app purchase.
The app must provide all material purchase information to the user prior to sale of any good or service and use Apple Pay branding and user interface elements correctly.
The app must disclose the length of the renewal term and that it continues until canceled, what is provided each period, the actual charges and how to cancel.
The app may only share user data acquired via Apple Pay with third parties to facilitate or improve delivery of goods and services.
Software offered under this rule must follow Guideline 3.1 in order to offer digital goods or services to end users.
